column1: #mapping_set_title: CALM to CAPEC attack pattern class mappings

#mapping_set_description: "Schema-level mappings between the FINOS Common Architecture Language Model (CALM 1.2) and the MITRE Common Attack Pattern Enumeration and Classification (CAPEC) LinkML schema. These mappings support threat modelling use cases: CALM Nodes are targets of CAPEC AttackPatterns; CALM Controls are mitigations that address CAPEC Categories; CALM ControlRequirements group into CAPEC Views. The mappings are relatedMatch because CALM is an architecture description language while CAPEC is a threat taxonomy - the relationship is an applicability mapping rather than a structural equivalence."

column7: A CALM Node is a bounded architecture element that may be the target of adversary activity; a CAPEC AttackPattern describes the method an attacker uses to exploit a vulnerability on a target - related as CALM Nodes are the targets that CAPEC AttackPatterns are applied against in a threat model.

A CALM Control is a domain-scoped safeguard applied to an architecture element; a CAPEC Category groups related attack patterns by a shared theme or target mechanism - related as CALM Controls are typically designed to address the attack patterns grouped under a CAPEC Category.

A CALM ControlRequirement defines the domain schema for a control domain; a CAPEC View is a curated subset or perspective on the CAPEC corpus for a specific stakeholder group - related as both provide a scoped, curated grouping of requirements or patterns for a specific audience or domain.

A CALM Architecture describes the surface area of a system that may be subject to attack; a CAPEC Category groups related attack patterns that apply to a class of systems - related as a CALM Architecture's node inventory determines which CAPEC Categories are applicable for threat assessment.
